profile: Backend engineer with 7+ years in PHP, specialising in Symfony and Domain-Driven Design. At plusForta (Areal Bank Gruppe) I led the modernisation of a legacy Symfony platform in a regulated banking environment, built GitLab CI/CD from scratch, cutting deployment from roughly 60 minutes to under 10, and introduced automated testing to a codebase that had none. Most recently I designed and shipped a production Progressive Web App end to end as sole engineer: Laravel backend, real-time multimodal transit routing, and a deterministic rules engine that reconfigures the application per user context. I own architecture decisions from data model through to deployment.

prologue.label: Prologue
prologue.summary: A computer science degree: the short time trial before the real race.

stages.label: Stage 1
stages.summary: First professional kilometres: Laravel e-commerce and ERP reporting for real businesses.
highlights: Built and deployed Laravel e-commerce platforms: product catalogues, cart and order management.
Integrated secure payment gateways with automated invoice generation.
Designed ERP reporting modules in raw SQL, bypassing the ORM for heavy data aggregation.

stages.label: Stage 2
stages.summary: Backend engineer on a large-scale SaaS recruitment platform serving enterprise clients.
highlights: Introduced Domain-Driven Design into a legacy PHP codebase, so the domain became testable on its own.
Replaced inefficient ORM paths with tuned raw SQL on high-traffic listing endpoints.
Shipped backend features for enterprise clients in retail and food service.

stages.label: Stage 3
stages.summary: Core engineer on a Symfony platform in a regulated, bank-owned environment.
highlights: Led the upgrade from a long-unsupported Symfony version, clearing years of technical debt and restoring security compliance.
Built GitLab CI/CD from scratch, replacing a manual process: release time from roughly 60 minutes to under 10.
Introduced automated testing with PHPUnit and Pest to a codebase with no coverage.
Profiled and fixed bottlenecks on critical paths; mentored developers through code review.

climbs.name: Symfony upgrade in a regulated bank

stages.label: Stage 4a
stages.summary: Designed, built and shipped a live PWA for everyday life and public administration in North Rhine-Westphalia, as the only engineer.
highlights: A deterministic, attribute-based rules engine: 24+ residence-permit scenarios validated against official sources.
Day Composer: a scheduler that builds a feasible day from constraints, opening hours and live travel times.
Real-time transit: MOTIS routing over live VRS GTFS-Realtime feeds, rendered with MapLibre.
Owned CI, deployment and production operations from first commit to public release.

climbs.name: Summit finish: a live product, solo

stages.label: Stage 4b
stages.summary: Designing and building a German vocabulary game where learning runs a café, as the only engineer: Laravel backend, spaced repetition and a 3D café.
highlights: FSRS-6 spaced repetition written in PHP and checked against the reference py-fsrs: 0 mismatches over 2,478 reviews.
Every answer is one database transaction with row locks and an idempotent event id, stored as an immutable review event.
A two-ledger design: only real reviews pay, practice pays nothing, and café levels come only from learning.
A 3D café in the browser, modelled from Python scripts in Blender.

climbs.name: Only learning pays: the two-ledger economy
FSRS-6 in PHP: 0 mismatches in 2,478 reviews
